title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Sequential and Ecological Program for Sustainable Resilience of the Sila Populations programme will work in Sila Province, Chad. It aims to contribute to Concern Chad's Green Graduation thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to ensure extremely poor and vulnerable households are more productive, can sustainably meet their basic needs and have improved coping strategies through strengthened livelihoods which place value on the natural environment. The programme will support over 110,970 people living in extreme poor households, subsistence farmers, pastoralists, female-headed households, households with disabled members. This will be done through ensuring access to a predictable and regular source of income to cover basic needs, increased access to basic services, improved knowledge of labour market opportunities, increased employment among participant households including in jobs focused on prevention or restoring the environment.. RM Adaptation 2: With this allocation, the green graduation (GG) programme in Chad will conduct a Climate Vulnerability and Capacity Assessment (CVCA) with the support of Head Office technical advisors. The purpose of the CVCA will be to support LTD GG communities to identify contextual climate shocks, stresses and changes that are impacting their ability to secure their basic needs. Communities will then be supported to develop Community Adaptation Action Plans (CAAPs) to address areas where communities can be empowered to make a positive difference in their resilience at the household or community level. The intention is that elements of these plans will be financed through the Climate Allocation in 2025. Gender equality 1: this is the main objective of the outcome, which is aimed at improving women’s participation and representation in targeted communities. DRR 1: Green Graduation programmes are intended to build the resilience of communities and natural systems to a changing climate through awareness raising, capacity building, environmental awareness and promoting climate-smart activities. Aid to Environment 1: Concern’s Green Graduation programme added a 5th pillar to the traditional graduation model - the ‘green’ aspect which aims to improve environmental protection and stability through awareness raising, capacity building, assessing environmental impacts, reducing and managing environmental risks and increasing natural assets. Capacity Building 1: building the capacity of communities on climate-smart activities is necessary for environmental protection and sustainability. Gender Equality 1: a gender lens is applied at every stage and a gender transformative approach is taken to tackle harmful gender norms, attitudes and practices. Nutrition 1: Through improved agricultural practices (increasing yields) and messaging on nutrition, the nutritional status of HHs is improved.
